dropped.finding: The `success` branch emits vote-type=success trusting WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION verbatim and never consults FAILURE_OBSERVED, so if the two failure signals ever diverge (aggregated conclusion=success while a needed job's result is failure/cancelled) the job casts Verified +1 despite an observed failure. The fail-closed cross-check is only wired into the `skipped` branch.

dropped.finding: No test pins the exact fail-closed output of the catch-all `*` branch for a non-empty unrecognized conclusion. The script documents `empty / anything else -> failure (fail-closed anomaly)`, but test_normalization_mapping asserts the exact value only for the empty string. The one test that exercises an arbitrary unknown value (`weird-value`) asserts only domain membership (`vote in {success,failure,cancelled}`), which a fail-OPEN regression (`* -> success`) would still satisfy. Since fail-open here lets a change vote itself Verified, this is the safety-critical behavior and it is untested for regressions.
merged_from: The `success` branch's documented independence from FAILURE_OBSERVED is not pinned: no test asserts the exact output for `("success", "true")`. The mapping states `success -> success` unconditionally, but the only `success` mapping case fixes `failure_observed=false`; `("success","true")` is exercised solely in the domain-membership test.
scenarios: A future edit changes the `*)` default from `vote="failure"` to `vote="success"` (fail-open); all tests still pass, and an anomalous/unrecognized conclusion silently casts Verified+1 on a change that never observed a green run.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add `("weird-value", "false", "failure")` and `("weird-value", "true", "failure")` to the test_normalization_mapping parametrize list so the catch-all's exact fail-closed value is pinned.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Fail-closed the `skipped` case (or treat cascaded-skip of required gate jobs as failure) so a run whose gates were SKIPPED cannot cast Verified+1.
evidence: scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh:48-55: `skipped)` branch -> `if [ "$failure_observed" = "true" ]; then vote="failure"; else vote="success"; fi`

.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:284: `FAILURE_OBSERVED: ${{ contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled') }}` — a `skipped` job result matches neither literal, so FAILURE_OBSERVED stays false when gates are skipped rather than failed

.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:254: `needs: [clear-vote, require-ticket, build-and-test, optionality, golden-path, verify-identity]` with `if: ${{ always() }}` (line 249) — dependent gate jobs are SKIPPED (not failed/cancelled) when an upstream `need` does not succeed

Reachability: skipped gates -> WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION=skipped + FAILURE_OBSERVED=false -> vote=success -> Verified+1 -> change becomes landable without the gates having executed (AGENTS.md contract: green CI must yield +1, but here CI never actually ran green)
dropped.finding: The `skipped -> success` branch is a fail-open path: when required gate jobs are SKIPPED (not failed) — e.g. an upstream `need` short-circuits so build-and-test/golden-path never run — WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION can be `skipped` while FAILURE_OBSERVED is `false` (a `skipped` job result matches neither 'failure' nor 'cancelled' in the contains() check), so the script emits `success` and casts Verified+1 even though the gates never actually passed.
scenarios: An upstream needed job (e.g. require-ticket) is skipped/short-circuited, cascading build-and-test and golden-path to `skipped`; im-open folds this to WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION=skipped; FAILURE_OBSERVED is false because no job is failure/cancelled; the change receives Verified+1 without its gates running.
dropped.suggested_fix: Treat `skipped` as fail-closed unless success is affirmatively established: fold a positive-success signal (e.g. require all required needs.*.result == 'success') into the decision, or map bare `skipped` to `failure` so an un-run gate set never yields Verified+1.
